description: An environmental compliance manager must approve the disposition and storage plan for 24 drums of solvent waste generated during a line-cleaning operation, including treatment quantities, retention controls, and the records required before removal from the plant.

shared_context.S1: Twenty-four drums of solvent waste from a recent line-cleaning operation are secured in the hazardous-waste cage.
shared_context.S2: The temporary storage permit for these drums expires on Friday.
shared_context.S3: Plant policy favors solvent recovery when the material meets the approved recovery specification and requires documented treatment for every drum removed from the cage.
shared_context.S4: The routine waste closeout requires the waste coordinator and production supervisor to submit their current records and required controls as recorded reports before Mara approves the disposition. A verbal summary does not substitute for the recorded report. Mara's approval follows immediately after both reports; no additional confirmation is required.

PF1.text: Jon received the laboratory classification report yesterday: 15 drums meet the approved solvent-recovery specification, 3 drums fail the water-content limit and must go to hazardous-waste incineration, and the remaining 6 drums were not classified in that report. A laboratory-system outage kept the report from being uploaded to the waste log.

PF2.text: Priya's completed batch-genealogy review identifies the 6 unclassified drums as drums from lot VX-204, which contain residual catalyst and must be retained on site for exactly 30 days for possible process investigation rather than sent for treatment. The hold tags have not yet been entered in the production system.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 9 drums must be assigned to solvent recovery after the 6-drum investigation hold is removed from the 15 recovery-eligible drums.
Exactly 3 drums must be assigned to hazardous-waste incineration.
Exactly 6 drums must be retained on site for exactly 30 days.
The three disposition categories must account for all 24 drums.
A recovery-dispatch record must be committed for 9 drums.
An incineration manifest must be committed for 3 drums.
Retention hold tags must be committed for 6 drums and 30 days.
The laboratory classification must be cited as justification after Jon submits the recorded report.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'recovery_dispatch' and c['count'] == 9 for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'incineration_manifest' and c['count'] == 3 for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'retention_hold_tags' and c['count'] == 6 and c['days'] == 30 for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The report changes the available treatment quantities to 15 recovery-eligible drums and 3 incineration drums, while the exact recovery count becomes 9 once the separate six-drum hold is applied.

The genealogy review changes six unclassified drums into an exact 30-day retention category, reducing recovery from 15 to exactly 9 and requiring six 30-day hold tags while preserving the 24-drum total.
